newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telmex rallies in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telmex rallies in heavy trade.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in Telefonos de Mexico, or Telmex, shot higher on Wednesday despite disappointing 1996 results.

The telephone company's ADRs jumped 1-1/4 to 40-1/4 in heavy trade. Volume was 3.7 million shares, making it the most active stock on the New York Stock Exchange. Telmex shares had fallen on Tuesday after reporting results well below those expected.
"The report initially looked pretty bad," a trader said, adding that investors had decided the results were better than first thought.
Among European ADRs, Dutch music and film company PolyGram NV rose 2-1/4 to 41-1/2 despite reporting lower 1996 earnings. It said sales growth in the music industry would recover strongly in 1997.
Swedish telecommunications company AB LM Ericsson was up 1/2 to 33-1/8 after its chief executive said the company planned to cut costs at its production plants and to increase its dividend.
Japanese car maker Nissan Motor Co Ltd slipped 1/8 to 12-5/8. Volume was 337,400 shares, well above normal daily trade, with most of the volume coming from two block trades.

Nissan, along with other Japanese companies that rely on exports, were seeing "strong buying by foreigners who believe there will be higher earnings" from the halt in the dollar's rise against the yen, a trader said.
Norway's Petroleum Geo-Services A/S rose 3/4 to 40-5/8 after it reported a 39 percent rise in 1996 net profits.
Advancers led decliners 314 to 194 among 807 ADRs. Volume was 51 million shares at midday.
